### The Sabbath Now and Not Yet
Author: Kim Riddlebarger
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/sabbath-now-and-not-yet
Passage: Hebrews 4:1
Points:
- The Christian life is an earthly pilgrimage moving toward an eternal rest with God.
- Israel's physical rest in Canaan was only a temporary type pointing to a greater heavenly city.
- The wilderness generation missed entering God's rest through unbelief, but Christ secures rest for believers.
- Christians enter God's rest today by ceasing from their own works and trusting solely in Jesus.
- The Lord's Day serves as a weekly foretaste of the future, consummate Sabbath in eternity.

### Rest for God's People
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/rest-gods-people
Passage: Hebrews 4:9-10
Points:
- The ultimate rest awaiting God's people is patterned after God's rest upon finishing creation.
- Divine rest is not inactivity, but God's supreme delight in Himself and His completed work.
- Believers in the final Sabbath will cease from earthly trials and actively serve and worship their King.
- Faith in Christ brings believers into spiritual rest now, though earthly sin still hinders its fullness.
- Setting aside weekly time for worship anticipates the unending joy of the eternal Sabbath.
